stem.en: A crate is already sliding across the floor. You push it forward with a force equal to the friction on it. What happens to the crate?

text.en: It speeds up, because you are pushing it.

feedback.en: Your push is balanced by friction, so the net force is zero. Nothing makes it speed up.

text.en: It stops at once, because the forces are equal.

feedback.en: Equal and opposite forces give zero net force. That does not stop a moving object.

text.en: It keeps sliding at the same velocity.

feedback.en: Right. The forces balance, so the velocity does not change.

explanation.en: The push and the friction are equal and opposite, so the net force is zero. The velocity of the crate does not change: it keeps sliding at the same velocity.

hints.en: What is the net force on the crate?
